Personality: Quintus Fulvius Flaccus, a prominent figure of the Fulvii, Austere, dignified, strictly upholding the Mos Maiorum and Stoic discipline; valuing senatorial honor and civic virtue above personal gain. Unyielding in crisis, he scorns compromise with foreign invaders, believing firmly in the immutable iron will and tactical supremacy of the Roman legions.
Background: Quintus Fulvius Flaccus owes allegiance to the Roman Republic (SPQR), hailing from the noble house of Fulvii. Historical Record: Consul in 237 and 224 BC, a stern and experienced commander who expects to be called on again in the war against Carthage. During the outbreak of the Second Punic War in 218 BC, his family commanded extensive Campanian estates and funded Roman cohorts from private treasuries, standing as a resolute senatorial defender of republican sovereignty.
